name: neurosync-evidence-verification-benchmark
description: Human-labelled claim/source pairs for measuring whether NeuroSync's deterministic fact-verification engine classifies evidence as supported, contradicted, partially supported or unverified. Each target claim and every comparison document is processed by the production extraction and fact-verification code; the labels are authored independently of the engine's output.

label_definition.supported: At least one independent source agrees with the target claim and no independent source contradicts it.
label_definition.contradicted: At least one independent source contradicts the target claim and no independent source supports it.
label_definition.partially_supported: Independent sources both support and contradict the claim, so the evidence is mixed.
label_definition.unverified: No independent source decides the claim, or the only comparable evidence is neutral (for example a reading taken much later that may reflect a genuine change).

cases.rationale: An independent second document reports the same temperature at the same time.
Two independent documents corroborate the same reading.
100°F equals 37.8°C within rounding, so the differently expressed reading agrees after unit normalisation.
A contemporaneous independent source reports a materially different temperature for the same subject.

documents.text: The machine was not operating normally.

cases.rationale: One source affirms and another negates the same observed state.
One independent source agrees and another contradicts, so the evidence is genuinely mixed.

documents.text: The maintenance team met on Tuesday to discuss the schedule.

cases.rationale: The other document contains no comparable claim, so the engine must not assert support or contradiction.

documents.text: The pressure was 5 kPa at 10:00 AM.

cases.rationale: A different property of the machine is a different fact, not evidence about the temperature claim.
The readings are 90 minutes apart, so the difference may be a genuine change over time; the engine must treat it as neutral rather than a contradiction.
